sources.researchNote: The file page dates the sitting to 1888 on the authority of Modest Tchaikovsky’s Life and Letters and records publication in 1904; the attribution to Reutlinger is given as an attribution, not as a signed credit. The image is a crop of a fuller cabinet card kept in the same collection. The composer enters the record here as the source of the themes arranged in the 1930 medley on which Kaper worked, so the likeness stands nearly forty years before that use.

media.title: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky — cabinet card portrait, 1888
media.description: Cabinet card portrait of Tchaikovsky taken in 1888 and attributed to the Paris photographer Émile Reutlinger, cropped to the figure from the full card.
media.altText: Studio portrait of the elderly Tchaikovsky in a dark coat, white-haired and bearded, turned slightly to his left.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph is attributed to Émile Reutlinger, who died in 1907, so the term of the author’s life and seventy years has long expired; it was also published in 1904, before the United States threshold of 1930. Attribution to the photographer and to the holding collection is retained.
